chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan and others, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, and I do not know Ibn Abi Hamza except that he also narrated it to me from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man has a male slave and a female slave, and this is known. He says, 'My slave and my slave girl have run away (escaped).' The judges compel him to provide two witnesses that this is his slave or his slave girl, who have not been sold nor given as a gift. We testify to this when compelled. He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَبَقَ: To run away or escape (specifically regarding slaves)
key_terms.لَمْ يَهَبْ: Has not been given as a gift

ai.seo_question: What is the legal requirement for a master to reclaim slaves who have run away according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the evidentiary burden in pre-modern Islamic jurisprudence regarding the reclamation of runaway slaves (*abq*). It establishes that while the master must present two witnesses to verify the slaves' identity and lack of transfer (sale or gift), the judicial process ultimately compels the master to affirm this testimony, reflecting the Shia emphasis on procedural fairness in property disputes. This mechanism ensures that masters cannot arbitrarily claim ownership without corroborating evidence, balancing the rights of the slave against the master's property claims.
